As one of the UK's largest academy trusts, we serve communities across the country, many facing significant challenges, supported by exceptional teachers, dedicated support staff and talented professionals who work behind the scenes to make it all possible. We are now looking for a Regional Finance Assistant to join our finance team, supporting three academies across London. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys working with numbers, thrives on accuracy and wants their work to have a meaningful impact.Our finance function supports 56 academies and more than 5,000 colleagues, making it a busy, varied and rewarding environment. You'll need to be organised, resilient and able to maintain high standards while managing competing priorities. Most importantly, you'll be a team player who enjoys collaborating with colleagues and solving problems. In this role, you'll support a wide range of financial processes, including purchase and sales ledgers, bank reconciliations, payroll administration, balance sheet accounts and transactional finance activity. Attention to detail will be your superpower. You'll take pride in ensuring invoices are processed accurately, payments are made on time, and financial records are maintained to the highest standards. The role is primarily home-based, with occasional visits to our London office at Devonshire House and academies across the region. This offers the flexibility to work independently while remaining connected to a supportive and experienced finance team.In return, you'll join a supportive and purpose-driven organisation where your contribution truly matters. We'll provide flexibility, development opportunities and the chance to learn from experienced finance professionals. Most importantly, you'll know that the work you do every day helps create better opportunities for young people and communities who need them most.We're looking for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, thrives on organisation and accuracy, and takes pride in keeping financial processes running smoothly. Ideally, you'll have experience in:Transactional finance processing, including purchase ledger, sales ledger, receipts and payments.Purchase ledger administration, including BACS payment runs, reconciliations, supplier account creation and managing debit balances.Sales ledger management, including raising and monitoring invoices and proactively following up outstanding debt.Bank account administration, including reconciliations, payment processing and maintaining accurate financial records.Finance systems administration, including creating accounts, resolving queries and supporting users.Providing wider finance support, from investigating credit card queries to assisting colleagues with ad hoc requests and projects.You'll be highly organised, comfortable managing competing priorities and able to maintain excellent attention to detail in a fast-paced environment.As the role supports academies and colleagues across the region, you'll also be willing and able to travel to Central London or Southampton for team meetings, training and academy visits when required.Most importantly, you'll bring a positive, can-do approach and a willingness to be part of a team that helps make a real difference to young people's lives.Ideally you will have worked and be familiar with accounting software such as PSF and be an advanced user of Excel. You’ll be reliable, accurate and willing to get stuck in as part of a collaborative and highly supportive team.What Oasis OffersWe know that talented finance professionals have plenty of choices. That's why, in return for your expertise and commitment, we offer a package that supports your wellbeing, professional growth and long-term financial security.A genuine work-life balance with flexibility and stability that can be hard to find in many finance roles.A supportive and collaborative culture, where colleagues work together, share expertise and celebrate success.The opportunity to do meaningful work, knowing your contribution helps improve the life chances of young people and supports communities across the country.Professional development opportunities to help you build your skills and progress your career within a national organisation.A competitive Local Government Pension Scheme, offering defined benefits, life assurance and valuable tax advantages.A generous annual leave entitlement, helping you maintain a healthy balance between work and personal life.Flexible and hybrid working arrangements, with the ability to work primarily from home alongside office and academy visits.Access to a national network of experienced finance professionals, providing support, collaboration and opportunities to learn from others within the Trust.Join Oasis Community Learning and use your financial skills to make a difference where it matters most.Closing date: 9am 18th Aug 2026This post is covered by Part 7 of the Immigration Act (2016) and therefore the ability to speak fluent and spoken English is an essential requirement for this rolePlease note: Oasis Community Learning does not accept unsolicited CVs or speculative introductions from recruitment agencies. eligibility_evidence.text: Fund or Department Description Carlyle’s European Private Credit team focuses on an Opportunistic / Hybrid Capital strategy called CCOF which is in fund III vintage with $20bn+ AUM following its launch in 2017. Carlyle’s CCOF strategy is seeking to provide funding or be a non-control investor in founder, family, management-led businesses that need capital for growth, M&A, capex, liquidity or special situations (80% of transactions). Instruments are varied and structures are tailor-made. The CCOF strategy occasionally caters to the needs of sponsor-owned businesses: junior debt, complex, transitional capital (20% of transactions). Target returns of 15-20%. In addition, the team has launched last year a European direct lending strategy which offers the opportunity to be part of a new strategy launch. Position Summary This opportunity is to work with the Private Credit team based in London. The role will involve providing analytical support to the team as they evaluate new investment opportunities throughout the UK and Continental Europe. This role will work alongside the team during the execution of new investments in these regions. The environment is fast-paced and demanding, with a strong emphasis on learning about investing and development as an investment professional within the Private Credit sectors. Candidates will work directly with senior investment professionals on the team and will be encouraged to be proactive and to take ownership of important projects. Primary Responsibilities The intern is expected, as part of a team and with guidance, to evaluate potential investment opportunities across a wide range of industries and geographies. They will be able to assess and present clearly the strengths and weaknesses of a potential investment, on both a quantitative and qualitative basis. In this role, you will; develop dynamic operating models, perform fundamental credit analysis, evaluate returns potential, optimal capital structure, and exit scenarios; develop and apply understanding of key aspects of loan and bond documentation, restructuring mechanics and insolvency regimes in various jurisdictions; analyze capital structure and various debt instruments to establish most attractive entry point, based on fundamental business valuation and downside protection analysis. On a typical day as an Intern, you will interact with advisors and management teams to evaluate and underwrite investment opportunities as part of due diligence processes; you will develop relationships with other market participants to identify general investment themes and specific opportunities; you will monitor existing investments including liaising with management and senior team members; and you will work on potential portfolio add-on acquisitions or refinancing transactions. By the end of the Internship, you will have developed a good understanding of capital structures and the potential levers for value creation, both financial and operational; you will have worked within the team to help present opportunities to investment committee. Requirements Education & Certificates Excellent academics in a related degree, such as Finance or Economics. Professional Experience Proven interest in a career in Investment Management; previous internship in similar industry preferred. Excellent excel skills; strong quantitative, credit, financial modelling and analytical skills; and a good understanding of financial and accounting valuation methods. Excellent research and due diligence skills with an aptitude for numeracy. Willing to take initiatives and drive the project forward to completion. Competencies & Attributes Excellent interpersonal skills are required as well as being and a team player. Self-starter; has confidence in asking questions and ability to work independently in a fast- paced environment with a willingness to learn. Understanding of key capital structure and credit concepts. Good communication and presentation skills. Tenacious/persistent – with a desire to go the extra mile. Mature and hard-working approach, strong executive presence. Solid organizational skills, high attention to detail and ability to prioritize. Personal and professional integrity of the highest order ​ ​ ​ About Us: The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG) is a global investment firm with $475 billion of assets under management, across 678 investment vehicles as of March 31, 2026. Founded in 1987 in Washington, DC, Carlyle has grown into one of the world's largest and most successful investment firms, with more than 2,500 professionals operating in 28 offices in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia. Carlyle’s purpose is to connect people, ideas, and capital to fuel growth for companies and performance for investors, which range from public and private pension funds to wealthy individuals and families to sovereign wealth funds, unions and corporations. Carlyle invests across three segments – Global Private Equity, Global Credit and Carlyle AlpInvest – and has deep expertise across industries, markets, and geographies. At Carlyle, we believe that a wide spectrum of experiences and viewpoints drives performance and success. Our CEO, Harvey Schwartz, has stated that, "To build better businesses and create value for all of our stakeholders, we are focused on assembling leadership teams with the strongest insights from a range of perspectives." Reflecting this view, emphasis is placed on development, retention and inclusion through our internal processes and seven Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). We cultivate a culture where ideas are openly shared and challenged, connecting diverse expertise and perspectives to drive enduring value.
